A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization and additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing experiments on three benchmarks, including performance comparisons, robustness tests, and ablations in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds routing-latency measurements and historical-data robustness results in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same ANNS feature estimation, random initial routing, one-time dual-weight optimization, and subsequent routing rule. Appendix D explicitly leaves its proposed traffic-aware extension to future work.

E1.justification: The three benchmarks remain unchanged. v2 adds two RouterBench test scenarios: corrupted historical labels and distribution shift using MMLU as historical data while evaluating on the other 12 data sources.

E2.justification: The same eight baselines remain in the original comparisons and appear in new Table 8. The new latency comparison uses five existing training-free baselines; no comparator is added or removed from a retained comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix C.5 adds post-embedding latency measurements at 4000–10000 queries and new corruption and cross-dataset protocols. Corruption uses 20% performance-label flips, cost jitter with sigma 0.25, and 3× spikes with 2% probability. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds two bounded RouterBench robustness tests examining dependence on historical-label quality and distribution matching. The existing arrival-order, deployment, budget, historical-data-size, embedding, and hyperparameter analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing repetition counts and error-bar figures are retained. Checklist item 7 restates reporting of variability across runs; Tables 7–8 introduce no additional run counts, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 7–8 add results: at 10000 queries, routing latency is 0.064 ms for Ours versus 0.203 ms for Greedy-Perf; Ours achieves performance scores of 2319.65 under noise and 2050.8 under distribution shift. Tables 1–6 and Figures 1–17 retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds Equation 8, defining a prospective service-capacity constraint using query service times, model backlog, and capacity within time windows. The original assumptions, theorem, lemmas, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central training-free online-routing contribution, conditional 1−o(1) competitive guarantee, and headline 3.55× performance, 1.85× cost-efficiency, and 4.25× throughput claims are retained. The added experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: v1 briefly suggests incorporating additional routing factors through constraints. v2 distinguishes query-intrinsic features from dynamic queue lengths and system load, explicitly places the latter outside the current formulation, and discusses future traffic-aware extensions. It also explains the exclusion of embedding from latency measurements.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and checklist statements that implementation and documentation are supplied. It documents the new timing and corruption experiments; the existing hardware, optimization solvers, and implementation details in Appendix A remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 66 cited works and substantive comparisons with prior routing and online-matching research are retained. Extended Related Work moves from Appendix D to Appendix E without a substantive change in novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Background becomes Section 1.1, subsequent sections are renumbered, and v2 adds a checklist, experimental subsection, traffic discussion, and broader-impact appendix. Limitations receive a localized rewrite, while most existing prose and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–8 and rearranges existing floats, including moving Table 1 into the evaluation discussion. Equations 5–6 become more compact. All 17 existing figures retain their plotted content rather than being redrawn.

improvement.justification: Tables 7–8 provide useful direct evidence about routing overhead and robustness to imperfect historical data beyond v1's evaluations. Clearer traffic-related limitations and code-access information also improve the paper. These gains are bounded: the new tests concern RouterBench, latency excludes embedding, and the core method, guarantees, and original results remain unchanged.
